newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end slightly lower.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended slightly lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.
"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields and bond prices were slightly lower but volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.74/1.69 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.80/1.75 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.90/1.85 percent against 1.95/1.90 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.49/98.54 from Monday's close of S$98.50/98.55, September 2001 at S$97.21/97.26 versus S$97.25/97.30 and June 2003 at S$95.23/95.28 against S$95.25/95.30.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 1-7/8 1-3/4 percent from Monday's 1-13/16 1-11/16 percent.
